Finqware Integrates Visa Direct Capabilities Into FinqTreasury to Modernise Global Money Movement
summary:
Finqware today announced a collaboration with Visa, a world leader in digital payments, designed to help mid-sized and large businesses manage global money movement more efficiently within the treasury workflows they already use every day.
Corporate finance teams often rely on multiple banking platforms, payment systems and FX providers to manage liquidity, payments and international money movement. Through this collaboration, Finqware will launch FX Hub, integrating cross-border payments and FX capabilities provided by Currencycloud, a Visa Direct offering, directly into FinqTreasury, enabling European corporates to manage these activities within a more connected treasury environment.
By leveraging FinqTreasury FX Hub-powered Currencycloud capabilities, businesses will be able to collect, hold, convert and send funds domestically and across borders from within the same platform used to oversee treasury operations. This enables finance teams to manage liquidity, payments and foreign exchange through a single workflow, helping reduce operational complexity and reliance on fragmented banking portals and payment systems.
Within FinqTreasury, corporate finance teams can manage multi-bank liquidity, execute domestic and cross-border payments, and access competitive FX capabilities while benefiting from greater visibility and control over how money moves across their organisation.
“Businesses increasingly need faster, more integrated ways to manage liquidity and move money around the world. Through this partnership, Finqware is integrating Currencycloud directly within the treasury workflows corporate finance teams already use every day. Together, we are helping businesses simplify international money movement, reduce operational friction and gain greater control over global cash management.” Zeynep Sayin, Head of Visa Direct Partnerships
The collaboration reflects a shared focus on helping businesses simplify treasury operations by bringing account information, payment initiation, FX and cross-border payment capabilities together within a single treasury environment.
By embedding Currencycloud, Finqware extends its treasury capabilities beyond domestic multi-bank operations into global money movement. Finance teams can access cross-border payments and FX capabilities alongside existing treasury processes, helping streamline day-to-day operations and improve efficiency.
“This partnership extends the capabilities available through FinqTreasury and helps simplify how businesses manage cross-border payments and FX. By combining Visa's global payment capabilities with Finqware's treasury management platform, we are helping businesses access international payments and FX capabilities within existing workflows. Together, we are making it easier for CFOs and Treasurers to manage liquidity across multiple banks and move money internationally from the same environment — with speed, low complexity and control.” Cosmin Cosma, CEO & Co-founder, Finqware
NoYesPayments15 Sep, 2026
content: Finqware has partnered with Visa to integrate Visa Direct and Currencycloud capabilities into its FinqTreasury platform. This collaboration introduces the FX Hub, allowing European corporate finance teams to manage multi-bank liquidity, cross-border payments, and foreign exchange within a single, unified workflow. The integration aims to reduce operational complexity and streamline global money movement for businesses.

Strategy copycat Satsuma crashed 99%, liquidated treasury
summary:
Mark Moss’ Satsuma Technology sold all 669 of its BTC and will return £30.7M after the company crashed 99% from its 2025 peak.
The post Strategy copycat Satsuma crashed 99%, liquidated treasury appeared first on Protos.
content: Satsuma Technology, inspired by MicroStrategy, saw its stock crash 99% from its 2025 peak. Led by Mark Moss, the company liquidated its entire treasury, selling all 669 Bitcoin. The firm announced plans to return £30.7 million to stakeholders following the dramatic collapse of its crypto-focused corporate strategy.

Mark Moss தலைமையிலான இந்நிறுவனம் தனது முழுமையான Bitcoin இருப்பையும் விற்றுள்ளது. இந்த கடுமையான வீழ்ச்சியைத் தொடர்ந்து, பங்குதாரர்களுக்கு £30.7 மில்லியன் தொகையைத் திருப்பப் போவதாக நிறுவனம் அறிவித்துள்ளது.

title: Adyen Joins Guidewire Marketplace as an Approved Global Payment Partner for Insurers
summary:
Adyen, the financial technology platform of choice for leading businesses, today announced that it has been approved as a Global Payment Partner for Guidewire. The integration will be launched through the Guidewire Marketplace, offering property and casualty (P&C) insurers a seamless way to connect Adyen’s payment capabilities with their Guidewire core systems.
The launch on the Guidewire Marketplace productizes the significant commercial momentum Adyen has already established within the insurance vertical. By choosing the Adyen integration, insurers can eliminate fragmented regional setups and manage the entire flow of funds throughout the policy lifecycle through a single global platform.
Enhancing the Insurer and Policyholder Experience
The Adyen integration functions as a vetted choice within the Guidewire Marketplace, allowing insurers to optimize front-end payment channels and back-end financial routing. Through this single integration, insurance leaders can seamlessly manage automated premium collections (including cards, ACH, and local payment methods), recurring billing retries, and efficient claims payouts utilizing bank transfers and virtual cards.
Differentiating with Intelligent Money Movement and Existing Market Traction
Unlike traditional payment processors or software-only layers that rely on third-party banks and fragmented regional networks, Adyen operates as a single platform with its own banking licenses. This allows the integration to handle the entire lifecycle of a transaction—from front-end acceptance to back-end clearing and settling—ensuring higher payout speeds, reduced transaction failure, and institutional-grade resilience.
“By launching our exciting integration on the Guidewire Marketplace, we are building upon the strong market leadership in the Insurance market that we’ve scaled in recent years,” said Adrian Davis, Managing Director Financial Services & Insurance at Adyen. “What differentiates Adyen is that we aren't just a software connection; we own the underlying financial infrastructure. As a global platform with our own banking licenses, we manage the full money movement stack end-to-end which ensures Guidewire’s customers easily offer whatever payment method their policyholders prefer, effectively turning payments from a legacy hurdle into a strategic advantage for growth.”
Advanced Security and Operational Efficiency
Insurers utilizing the marketplace integration will be able to leverage Adyen’s full money movement stack across Guidewire’s customer base of more than 570 insurers across 43 countries. Key features of the integrated solution include:
True End-to-End Processing: Eliminates third-party banking intermediaries, resulting in faster financial routing and reduced operational costs.
Unified Reporting: Access to centralized transaction data and automated reconciliation to streamline back-office operations.
Built-in Fraud Protection: Utilization of Adyen's machine learning risk engine to identify and mitigate fraudulent insurance activity.
Data Security: Advanced tokenization capabilities to keep card-on-file data continuously secure and compliant.
The integration is available globally, allowing insurers across North America, Europe, LATAM, and APAC to leverage the solution after launch in 2027 . Because the integration is standardized for the Guidewire Marketplace, it can be implemented by any Global Systems Integrator (GSI) or an insurer’s internal IT team, ensuring maximum flexibility during deployment.

GISEC GLOBAL 2026 Opens Tomorrow in Dubai as Global Cyber Leaders Converge to Shape the Next Digital Era
summary:
GISEC Global 2026, the Middle East and Africa’s largest cybersecurity event, opens tomorrow at Dubai Exhibition Centre (DEC), Expo City, at a time when artificial intelligence, geopolitical tensions and increasingly sophisticated attacks on critical infrastructure are driving unprecedented demand for international cybersecurity collaboration.
Now in its 15th edition, GISEC Global is positioning Dubai as a key meeting point for the cybersecurity community, as governments and businesses confront a rapidly evolving threat landscape shaped by artificial intelligence, geopolitical tensions and accelerating digital transformation. The continued growth of GISEC Global reflects increasing international demand for collaboration, with governments, regulators and technology leaders choosing Dubai as the platform to shape the next generation of cyber resilience.
Held under the theme Cyber First: The New Digital Order, GISEC Global 2026 is hosted by the UAE Cyber Security Council, with the Dubai Electronic Security Center (DESC) participating as the event's official Government Cybersecurity Partner. The event is also supported by the Ministry of Interior and Dubai Police. Running until September 18, GISEC Global welcomes participants from 182 countries, serving as a global convergence point for government leaders, national cyber authorities, enterprise CISOs, technology innovators, ethical hackers and the next generation of cybersecurity professionals.
Global Cyber Leadership Converges in Dubai
A defining new addition to this year’s edition is the Cyber First Global Summit, where ministers, central bank governors, national cybersecurity authorities, CEOs and global institutions will examine the growing interdependence between cybersecurity, economic stability and national security. The summit will craft the future of cyber-first economies, where secure digital infrastructure and technological sovereignty are becoming essential to long-term resilience and economic continuity.
The show will also feature prominent cybersecurity leaders from across government and industry, including H.E. Dr Mohamed Al Kuwaiti, Head of UAE Cyber Security Council; H.E. Amer Sharaf, CEO of Cyber Security Systems and Services Sector at Dubai Electronic Security Center (DESC); Subra Kumaraswamy, Senior Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer at Visa; Alex Attumalil, Global Chief Information Security Officer at Under Armour; and Roeland Delrue, Co-Founder and COO of Aikido Security. Their participation reflects the progressively global and cross-sector nature of cyber challenges facing governments and businesses.
From AI-enabled Cybercrime to Identity Fraud
The cybersecurity landscape is evolving faster than traditional defence models can adapt. AI is giving cybercriminals new ways to scale and refine attacks, with 60 per cent of ransomware campaigns now reported to be fully AI-assisted. Polymorphic malware further complicates the threat landscape by continuously altering its code, making it harder for traditional security systems to identify and contain malicious activity. 
Deepfakes are emerging as a critical dimension of AI-enabled cybercrime, blurring the line between legitimate and fraudulent digital identities. The Entrust 2026 Identity Fraud Report, based on more than one billion identity verification events across 195 countries, found that deepfakes accounted for one in five biometric fraud attempts. 
As organisations grapple with the implications of AI-powered identity fraud and digital manipulation, GISEC Global will bring the issue into sharp focus through a keynote session featuring Michael Kelly, the four-time Emmy Award-nominated actor best known for his role as Doug Stamper in House of Cards. His session will explore the growing threat posed by deepfakes, digital identity and AI-powered impersonation, examining how technology is reshaping trust in an increasingly digital world.
Technology, Talent, and Readiness Take Centre Stage
GISEC Global 2026 will showcase emerging technologies across AI, quantum computing and OT/ICS, alongside live cyber drills and international cooperation forums that put cyber readiness to the test. The event will also place a strong emphasis on the people shaping cyber defence through programs including Women in Cyber, North Star Startups, Mentorship Labs.
The programme will also feature the Dubai Cyber Challenge, held under the patronage of His Highness Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Chairman of the Dubai Ports and Borders Security Council, with DESC supporting the School of Cyber Defense in collaboration with its programme partners. Meanwhile the GISEC CISO Circle will gather more than 250 cybersecurity leaders for closed-door briefings and collaboration.
Building Sovereign Resilience in a Fragmented Digital World
As geopolitical tensions and cyber-driven threats reshape digital borders, governments are prioritising sovereign capabilities to protect national data, critical infrastructure and technological independence. From sovereign cloud environments and localised AI to post-quantum readiness, the next phase of AI preparedness will largely depend on a country’s ability to secure the technologies and systems supporting its economy.
GISEC Global 2026 will accelerate the world’s shift from reactive cybersecurity to ecosystem-wide resilience, uniting policymakers, security leaders and technology innovators to strengthen critical infrastructure, advance responsible AI governance and build digital trust. As governments and industry confront increasingly complex cyber threats, 
GISEC Global 2026 reinforces Dubai's position as a leading international hub for cybersecurity collaboration, innovation and digital resilience.

content: GISEC Global 2026 opens tomorrow at the Dubai Exhibition Centre, uniting global cyber leaders, government officials, and technology innovators. Now in its 15th edition and hosted under the theme 'Cyber First: The New Digital Order', the event addresses rising threats from AI-enabled cybercrime, deepfakes, and attacks on critical infrastructure. The gathering highlights international cooperation, sovereign resilience, and cutting-edge security solutions to shape the next digital era.
